entries.title: White House denies Hegseth and Rubio to leave jobs after Republican election losses
entries.snippet: US media reports there are calls to replace Pete Hegseth, who also faces a possible impeachment vote, while Marco Rubio is rumoured to be eyeing a presidential run.

entries.title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument
entries.snippet: The order comes after Trump made a series of big changes to the decor of the Oval Office and tore down the White House East Wing.

entries.title: Two dead after bus crashes in France, officials say
entries.snippet: One child and one young adult were killed in the crash, local authorities say, with more injured.

entries.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
entries.snippet: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".

entries.title: Pope begins lengthy trip to Latin America weeks after lung cancer surgery
entries.snippet: Pope Leo, who had part of a lung removed last month, will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

entries.title: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of inciting unrest but acquitted of treason
entries.snippet: The 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, says the charges are politically motivated.

entries.title: Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for Cybertruck
entries.snippet: Musk said it was to make room for production of its Cybercabs - autonomous taxis without a driver.

entries.title: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
entries.snippet: The country's first nationwide elections since 1969 are due next year - a timetable now thrown into doubt.

entries.title: Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest
entries.snippet: Evidence of digging and new buildings are visible in satellite imagery taken in November, satellite images suggest.

entries.title: California governor commutes sentences for state's 548 death row inmates
entries.snippet: California has historically had the largest population of people on death row in the US.

entries.title: Nigerian court rules opposition candidate cannot stand in elections
entries.snippet: The high court has sacked the leadership of the opposition ADC party with only months to go until elections.

entries.title: Macau jails pro-democracy campaigner in city's first national security case
entries.snippet: Au Kam San was sentenced to 12 years and six months' jail for "subversion against the political power of the state".

entries.title: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
entries.snippet: The move follows a bank collapse and after the lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial against him.

entries.title: Hoax bomb threats target European airlines and airports for second time in a week
entries.snippet: At least 21 flights across Europe are affected in what the UK government calls a "malicious hoax threat".

entries.title: French protests see numbers surge as unions join strikes over high cost of living
entries.snippet: The interior ministry estimates 600,000 people joined protests across France, while the unions say the number was far higher.

entries.title: Democratic socialist defeats incumbent Karen Bass in Los Angeles mayor's race
entries.snippet: The results mean America's two most populous cities - New York and Los Angeles - will be led by democratic socialists.

entries.title: Eight killed in series of shootings in western Turkey
entries.snippet: Victims are found in several locations in three separate vehicles, according to local reports.

entries.title: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
entries.snippet: The US first lady was credited by all for playing a key though unspecified role in the ceasefire.

entries.title: Bomb hoaxes: Messages reveal how threat was passed on by air traffic control
entries.snippet: BBC Verify has been analysing messages after flights across Europe were targeted by fake bomb threats - the second such incident this week.

entries.title: Chris vs Chris: Who's running and what's at stake this New Zealand election
entries.snippet: New Zealanders will head to the polls on 7 November to elect a new government, with rising cost of living a key concern for voters.

entries.title: Why gold prices are surprisingly low
entries.snippet: Gold tends to go up when there's uncertainty in the economy. For a while, the price reflected that. But this week, it dropped from a nearly $5,600 in January to below $4,000. What's going on?

entries.title: Past White House adviser Raj Panjabi has written a playbook for 'living room' crises
entries.snippet: Dr. Raj Panjabi is the author of Safer: A Playbook. His goal is to help people face a personal crisis — health, workplace, family conflicts — and "turn fear into action."

entries.title: Low birth rates were emptying public schools. ICE deportations are now making it worse
entries.snippet: School enrollment was already expected to plunge by 2 million kids by 2030. Education experts say deporting immigrant families, many with school-age children, is making the crisis worse.

entries.title: Fill in the blank in the quiz: Vance says they lost the midterms because of ____
entries.snippet: Plus: Heidi Klum's hand, hackers and the pope's visitor!

entries.title: Morning news brief
entries.snippet: The Labor Department to release October jobs report Friday, what tactics are available to the Democratic Party to bring down fuel prices, judge blocks construction of Trump's arch for 14 days.

entries.title: Former Army medic reflects on his toughest moments helping the wounded
entries.snippet: Twenty years ago, Army Staff Sergeant Phillip Trezza deployed to Iraq as a medic. He speaks with his teenage daughter about some of his toughest moments.

entries.title: After cancer surgery, Pope Leo embarks on Latin America trip
entries.snippet: Pope Leo XIV is kicking off a three-nation tour of Latin America with a visit to Uruguay, three weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery that had put the entire trip into question.

entries.title: A judge blocks construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval
entries.snippet: The Trump administration hoped to begin construction immediately after a federal panel approved its arch late Thursday. But just after midnight, the judge issued an order blocking work for 14 days.

entries.title: Fears of an AI crackdown after midterms spark $2 trillion rout in tech stocks
entries.snippet: Shares sank, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping over 5%, as investors reacted with fear that a Democratic Congress — and states across the country -— would crack down on AI and data centers.

entries.title: These are the races in the House and Senate that haven't been called yet
entries.snippet: Democrats are poised to have a strong majority in the upcoming Congress. The final numbers are still being determined. Here's where things stand in the races that are waiting to be called by the AP.

entries.title: Alabama executes man for 1991 killings in last of 3 U.S. executions carried out the same day
entries.snippet: Florida carried out a record-tying 19th execution of the year in an unusual instance of three states administering the death penalty on the same day.

entries.title: 'JD, habibi.' Arabs celebrate El-Sayed's use of a term of affection in his victory speech
entries.snippet: "Habibi" literally translates to "my beloved" and is peppered through Arab pop songs. In everyday speech, it often means "buddy," "pal," or "bro." El-Sayed's supporters have sported shirts reading "Habibi for Abdul."

entries.title: Tankers carrying Russian diesel change course, raising doubts about shipments to U.S.
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump's plan to allow imports of Russian diesel appeared to falter this week after state and federal officials warned that handling any shipments could bring legal consequences and two tankers initially bound for the United States changed course.

entries.title: A look at the midterm races that remain undecided
entries.snippet: As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress and Republicans grapple with stunning losses, every remaining race matters. Some races are still too close to call, including Senate battles in both Alaska and Mississippi. Congressional correspondent Lisa Desjardins reports.

entries.title: After midterms, Trump is left to weigh his next move in Iran war that contributed to GOP loss
entries.snippet: As Trump ponders his next move, the stakes couldn't be higher for Iran, the Middle East and the global economy writ large.

entries.title: After midterms, world leaders await Trump's next move in Iran
entries.snippet: Tuesday's election results were not just closely watched in the U.S. American elections, in many ways, have become global events and the Democratic wave led to an extraordinary outpouring. Nick Schifrin gauges that reaction.

entries.snippet: California Gov. Gavin Newsom commuted the state's entire death row population to life in prison without parole. The decision could grant clemency to 548 people. Newsom had previously put a moratorium on executions in the state in 2019, but left hundreds on death row. Amna Nawaz d

entries.title: Rep. Garcia says voters gave Democrats a mandate to pursue accountability
entries.snippet: With Democrats set to take control of the House, they are making plans to use their majority not only to advance legislation but also to ramp up congressional oversight. California Rep. Robert Garcia is expected to become the new chairman of the House Oversight Committee. He says

entries.title: Refugee influx and foreign aid cuts strain South Sudan's health care system

entries.title: Hegseth allows National Guard to boost DC patrols with military vehicles, boats and patrol cars
entries.snippet: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has signed off on the National Guard ramping up its presence in the nation's capital in military vehicles and boats as troops deepen their integration with local law enforcement.

entries.title: State lawmakers seek greater control over what universities can teach
entries.snippet: Democrats in Texas will head to Austin with power they haven't had in decades. One of the many questions is whether they will try to reverse changes made at universities in recent years by Republicans. Texas is not alone. More than half of all college students are enrolled in a s

entries.snippet: D.L. Hughley is one of comedy's most enduring stars. His new memoir, "Charlie's Boy," offers a candid look at fatherhood, family trauma, and the path he took from South Central LA to some of the biggest stages on the planet. Geoff Bennett spoke with Hughley about all that and mor

entries.title: Paraguay prosecutor will seek charges against embattled president after bank collapse
entries.snippet: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña is under criminal investigation following the collapse of a major digital bank, prosecutors announced, hours after the South American leader's resignation and impeachment Thursday.

entries.title: After taking control of Congress, Democrats vow major probes into Trump's 'tentacles of corruption'
entries.snippet: Corruption topped the list of concerns for voters who ousted Republicans and handed Democrats control of Congress in the midterm elections. Now, the newly empowered Democratic Party is putting the issue front and center as its leaders chart their course for investigations and pol

entries.title: Elon Musk gambled $445 million to boost Republicans in the midterms. It came up short
entries.snippet: Nobody may have suffered bigger losses Tuesday than President Donald Trump. But few others had more on the line than Musk, who gambled big and came up holding the midterm's worst return on investment.

entries.title: What happens when airlines receive bomb threats?
entries.snippet: Hundreds of airline passengers in Europe had their flights diverted or given military escorts this week after a series of bomb threats that officials have said were malicious hoaxes.

entries.title: WATCH: First lady Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian officials. Trump met with Putin's envoy
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump said he met with Vladimir Putin's envoy at the White House on Thursday but did not meet with Ukrainian officials who were also visiting.

entries.title: Trump makes the Oval Office a national monument, but future presidents can still redecorate
entries.snippet: It was the third day this week that the president, a real estate mogul, delivered remarks fixated on his pet projects in Washington.

entries.title: Key federal panel expected to approve Trump's arch amid court challenge
entries.snippet: The approval would clear a hurdle on the road to breaking ground on the project, and the administration has said it could launch construction within a day of the vote. But the proposed 250-foot tall gilded arch still faced legal challenges.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: India: Why does Delhi keep failing to tackle its air pollution crisis?
entries.snippet: Despite years of government interventions, emergency restrictions and public outrage, Delhi continues to battle dangerously polluted air every winter. Why isn't there a lasting solution to a predictable crisis?

entries.title: Kenya cult leader Paul Mackenzie sentenced to 200 years
entries.snippet: A court in Kenya has sentenced Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and an adult. He told them to starve themselves to death as part of his apocalyptic religious cult.

entries.title: Exercise and cancer: What "living longer" really means
entries.snippet: A major trial found more colon cancer patients were alive eight years after treatment with long-term exercise coaching. But what does "living longer" mean, and who does it apply to?

entries.title: Turkey: Ex-minister arrested in a major fund manipulation scandal
entries.snippet: Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya, a former deputy chair of President Erdogan's party, was arrested in a major funds scandal. The opposition claims Sayan Kaya and her husband cashed in shares worth millions in the illegal scheme.

entries.title: French bus carrying school children crashes, killing 2
entries.snippet: The bus reportedly veered off the road and crashed into a tree. French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot was on his way to the scene.

entries.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
entries.snippet: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

entries.title: Pope Leo sets off on 12-day South America tour
entries.snippet: The pontiff will hold meetings and celebrate Mass in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, with the latter attracting particular interest. The trip will be the longest and farthest of his papacy so far.

entries.title: Malaysia: Ex-leader Najib seeks to leave prison for house arrest
entries.snippet: Convicted for embezzlement, former Prime Minister Najib Razak hopes to serve his prison term under house arrest after his party paid a fine. But the attorney general later said his transfer was on hold temporarily.

entries.title: Germany news: Trial of alleged 'Reichsbürger' group ringleaders begins
entries.snippet: Four members of the banned far-right "Kingdom of Germany" are on trial for belonging to a criminal organization. Meanwhile, a new study warns data centers could lead to water stress in Germany. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: India: Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam go back to Supreme Court for bail
entries.snippet: Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have asked the Supreme Court for bail once more, having spent over six years in jail. Elsewhere, the top court has clarified when the 24-hour clock for producing an arrested person starts.

entries.title: US judge temporarily blocks Trump's arch project after panel approval
entries.snippet: A judge ordered a two-week stop to construction on US President Trump's arch project in Washington. A federal panel had approved Trump's triumphal arch plans in an 8-4 vote.

entries.title: Ex-lawmaker jailed in Macau's first national security trial
entries.snippet: Pro-democracy former lawmaker Au Kam San was found guilty of "subversion against the political power of the State." He was handed a prison sentence of 12-and-a-half years.

entries.title: Trump raises prospect of 'big, beautiful' Russia-Ukraine deal
entries.snippet: US President Donald Trump said the Ukraine war was close to being settled and that ending it might involve "all of Europe." Trump has previously made several similar promises, with no resolution to the conflict in sight.

entries.title: Austrian tycoon Rene Benko sentenced to 2 years in prison for fraud
entries.snippet: Austrian businessman Rene Benko, who suffered a major fall from grace after his real estate empire, Signa Holding, went bust, was handed two more years in prison.

entries.title: Gavin Newsom commutes sentences of all death row inmates in California
entries.snippet: Gavin Newsom, a Democrat and a rumored presidential candidate, moved to commute the death sentences of 548 inmates in California for one of his last acts as governor of the state.

entries.title: Americans voted against Trump's Iran war. Gulf countries hope that means an end to the conflict
entries.snippet: The US midterm results showed how unpopular Donald Trump's Iran war is. Now, Gulf countries, trapped for months in the middle of the war between the US and Iran, see reason for optimism.

entries.title: Pete Hegseth under fire as Republicans trade blame for midterm debacle
entries.snippet: Iran war hawk Pete Hegseth is facing the fallout from Republicans' midterms losses as high energy prices turned voters toward Democrats. US President Trump continues to support his embattled defense chief — for now.

entries.title: Does the Oleshky ceasefire signal progress to come in Ukraine?
entries.snippet: Hundreds of civilians were evacuated from the city of Oleshky after Russia and Ukraine agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire. Some observers have expressed optimism that more such humanitarian missions might follow.

entries.title: France: More than 600,000 protest as anger grows over cost of living
entries.snippet: Demonstrators took to the streets in several French cities to call for government action on the high cost of living. Protests were largely peaceful, but there were some reports of escalation, including in Paris.
